availability.body: Instead of searching the board, you can say when you have time: the whole festival, the same hours every day, or a few single dates. Pick one, the grid below changes to match, then save. Organisers see it while they plan, so nobody asks you about mornings you were never free anyway.
availability.title: Or let the shifts find you

bookIt.body: One press books it, with no form and no approval step. The block turns green for you, and the count goes up for everybody else. If something comes up, the same press hands it back. Try it if you like; the tour carries on either way.
bookIt.title: Taking it is one press

finish.body: Jobs are split into shifts, you take the ones that suit you, and your availability covers the rest. The buttons here take you straight to the jobs and to your own shifts. Feel free to look around; the demo is yours until the timer runs out.
finish.title: That's the tour

jobRow.body: On the left is the job itself: its name, where it happens, and how many places are still free. The rest of the row is the same job spread across the festival days, and each small block in it is one shift. Scroll down the page to see where people are still missing.
jobRow.title: One row, one job

jobsIntro.body: A job is something that has to be covered over a stretch of time, like a welcome desk all weekend or a café counter on the Saturday. Each job is split into shifts, and a shift is what you sign up for. This screen shows both.
jobsIntro.title: Jobs, and the shifts in them

myBookings.body: Your past and upcoming shifts, each with the time, the place and the people working alongside you, which is what you need on the morning itself. This is also where you hand a shift back if plans change. The next step shows how to find shifts that suit you.
myBookings.title: Everything you said yes to

nextShift.body: You are already signed up for a few shifts, and the next one is always at the top: when it starts, where to go, and who else will be there. Most helpers come to this page just to check that. The next screen shows where these shifts come from.
nextShift.title: What you are already down for

openChip.body: Each block is one shift. The start time is on top, and below it the places taken out of the places needed. This one still has room. Pale blocks are full and green ones are yours, so you can read a whole weekend without opening anything. Press below and I'll open this one for you.
openChip.title: A shift with room in it

shiftRoster.body: Each shift is a small group of people. The list shows who has already said yes, and the blank line is the place that is still free. Seeing that others are already in often makes the decision easier. Where to go and what to bring are shown just above.
shiftRoster.title: Who is already on it

attention.body: Riverside Summer Festival is half staffed, and this panel shows what needs you now: shifts nobody has taken, shifts still short of people, and anyone waiting to join. Each line shows a count and links straight to it, so you can work through the panel like a to-do list. When nothing needs doing, the panel disappears.
attention.title: What needs you right now

finish.body: Describe a job once, let wirksam split it into shifts, keep an eye on the ones short of people, and check afterwards how it went. Everything you've seen works the same way in a real event, and the person who asked to join is still waiting. Feel free to look around; the demo is yours until the timer runs out.
finish.title: That is the whole loop

formIntro.body: You create a job on this one page, in five sections: what the job is, which event it belongs to, which days it runs, how each day is split up, and a preview. The first two are already filled in so the rest has something to work with, and I'll open the others one at a time. Nothing is saved until you save it.
formIntro.title: One form, one job

generateShifts.body: Set the daily time window, how long one shift lasts, and how many people it needs. From these three, wirksam works out every shift on every day you picked, down to the odd half hour left at the end. Change the shift length and watch the count in the preview change. This step saves you typing forty rows by hand.
generateShifts.title: This is where shifts come from

jobRow.body: A job is something that has to be covered over a stretch of time, like a welcome desk all weekend or a café counter on the Saturday. You describe it once, on the left of this row. wirksam does the rest and splits the job into single shifts, day by day.
jobRow.title: One row, one job

people.body: Each row is someone who can see the schedule, and the role next to their name says what they can do: members take shifts, admins also plan, and the event owner can hand the event over to someone else. Above is the person from the dashboard who is still waiting to join. Accept them and they can start taking shifts right away. The invitation card below is view only, because the demo doesn't send email.
people.title: The people in your event

reporting.body: How much of the schedule was filled, how many hours people gave, who took on the most, and which times of day were hardest to cover. Next to it is a spreadsheet export if you'd rather do your own sums. It helps in the week after, and even more when you plan next year.
reporting.title: How it actually went

shiftPreview.body: Here you see every shift your settings would create, counted and listed, before any of them exist. Tap one to leave it out, such as a Sunday morning nobody works. Fixing a two-hour block that should have been one hour is easy now and a lot of trouble once forty people have booked into it. The save button is at the bottom; the tour leaves that one to you.
shiftPreview.title: Check before you save

staffing.body: Each block shows the places taken out of the places needed, so you can check a whole weekend's staffing by scrolling down the page. This one is still short of people; the pale ones are full. That's your list for the week before, and volunteers see exactly the same board. Next is the form all of this was created from.
staffing.title: Reading the schedule at a glance

taskDates.body: A single day, a run of days, or a few separate dates across the event. Separate dates suit a festival with gaps, like this one. A short run inside the event's dates is already picked, which is why the calendar offers nothing outside them. Everything you set after this applies to each of those days.
taskDates.next: How the day is cut up
taskDates.title: Which days it runs
